To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the overall topology of the AAV serotype-8 (AAV-8) viral capsid structure is similar to that of AAV2, with an eight stranded β-barrel and a long loop between the β-strand, and that the most significant differences are located on the surface at the two-, three- and five-fold axes.

we determined the structure of adeno-associated virus serotype 8, which has a significantly greater liver-transduction efficiency than other serotypes, and we found that the most significant differences between this serotype and the previously studied adeno-associated virus 2 are located on the viral capsid surface.

the structure of AAV8, a promising gene therapy vector, has been solved to 2.5 Å and that the capsid surface amino acid differences with AAV2 are consistent with the known differences in their biological properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and use of adeno-associated viral vectors (AAVs) for the gene therapy of human genetic diseases.
the development of new gene therapy vectors based on the adeno-associated virus (AAV).
the structure and function of adeno-associated viruses (serotypes 2, 4, 8, 9) and the use of these viruses as gene therapy vectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

AAV8 is a gene therapy vector with a structure that is similar to AAV2, but with some significant differences in the capsid surface amino acid distribution that are consistent with its unique properties as a gene therapy vehicle.
the structure of the AAVA8 capsid provides a platform for mutagenic studies that may lead to the design of improved AAV vectors for gene therapy.
the structure of AAV8 is very similar to AAV2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have determined the structure of the capsid of AAV8 to 2.8 Å resolution, and have compared it to the previously solved structures of AAV1, AAV2, AAV3, and AAV4.
we have solved the structure of AAV serotype eight (AAV8), a promising gene therapy vector, to a resolution of 2.6 Angstroms.
AAV serotype capsid structure is important for understanding their tissue tropism, transducing efficiency, and antibody recognition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AAV8 is an excellent vector for in vivo gene delivery.
the AAV8 structure will be useful in understanding the structure-function relationships for the AAVs.
we now have the structural basis for understanding the differences in tissue tropism and immune response between different AAV serotypes.
